title: Rugby union coach apologises for pushing and swearing at TV presenter during broadcast
content:
The coach of one of England’s leading rugby union clubs has apologised for pushing and swearing at a television presenter live on air.

Geoff Parling, the head coach of Leicester Tigers, was involved in a heated confrontation with Craig Doyle, the lead presenter of UK broadcaster TNT Sports’ rugby coverage, before the Slater Cup match against Gloucester at Villa Park stadium, home of English football club Aston Villa.

The incident was sparked when Doyle invited pundit Liam MacDevitt, a former footballer turned broadcaster, to try and score a penalty through the posts under which Leicester’s players were warming up.

The stunt was devised as an initiation for MacDevitt, who was making his first appearance as a rugby presenter on TNT, which also televises the Gallagher Premiership, England’s flagship club competition.

MacDevitt missed the kick, with the ball landing near Leicester’s squad behind the posts, prompting Parling to walk over to confront the broadcasters.

Doyle, believing Parling was intending to chat to him, jokingly asked the former England international whether he “would sign” MacDevitt. But Parling, 42, failed to see the funny side, shoving Doyle towards the perimeter pitch and saying, “That’s not on. That’s f***ing not on. Get off the pitch.”

Doyle apologised to viewers for the bad language as he and MacDevitt made their way off the field, also remarking that Parling, who won 29 England caps in his playing career, was “clearly not happy about that.”

When asked about the incident after the match — which Leicester won 36-17 — Parling said his irritation stemmed from safety concerns.

“The producer from TNT has just come and apologised to me,” he told reporters. “They had something set up that wasn’t passed with anybody without our knowledge.

“I’m very wary. We need to protect my players, and certainly balls flying towards our players that could go anywhere, where there’s an injury risk, and I’m obviously not going to be happy.”

On Sunday, however, Leicester released a statement apologising for Parling’s behaviour.

It read: “Whilst this was contrary to standard practise and — as always — the well-being of those players under the posts was Geoff Parling’s primary concern, Leicester Tigers and Geoff Parling accept that the response was unnecessary and would like to apologise unreservedly to everyone involved.”

In the statement, Parling said: “I would like to apologise for the incident pre-game yesterday — it is important we stay a family-focused game and it wasn’t appropriate for viewers to see that.

“We have a great product in the Gallagher Premiership and I offer my thanks to Craig Doyle and everyone at TNT for continuing to innovate and think differently. After talking last night we’ll make sure we are fully aligned behind new ideas, including when best to use them; and keep pushing our game to new audiences.”

Leicester said they had also offered private apologies to TNT staff at Villa Park from Parling and the club.
